page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance belonging to the ecs.gn6i family. It is equipped with 24 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. The instance includes 93.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single bundled NVIDIA T4 GPU from the Turing architecture family, which features 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included on this instance, and network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside a poor rating in single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks also register in the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is weak. The standout capability of this hardware configuration lies in its LLM inference performance, where prompt processing speeds for both small and medium models reach top-tier levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated computing. By pairing a mid-range NVIDIA T4 GPU with a moderate allocation of system memory and dedicated vCPUs, it avoids the higher resource density costs associated with top-tier accelerator platforms. This makes it suitable for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration but do not require massive parallel memory bandwidth or high-frequency single-core CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include small to medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and general-purpose GPU-assisted tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 24 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, 93.0 GB of system memory, and a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-hypervised server does not include local storage and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data reveals a performance tradeoff: while single-core CPU and memory performance are weak, multi-core CPU metrics and memory bandwidth remain average. Crucially, the bundled NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers top-tier prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM models, alongside strong text generation performance for 7B models. This hardware profile makes the instance a cost-efficient choice for GPU-assisted workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, and image processing, where high-end single-core CPU performance is not a primary requirement.
